long_how_credit_scores_quietly_determine.title: How Credit Scores Quietly Determine Your Financial Options

scenes.label: Numerical Expression
scenes.line: A credit score is a numerical expression derived from an analysis of an individual credit history and credit report. Lenders use credit scores to evaluate the risk of lending money to consumers.
scenes.image_prompt: A modern computer screen displaying graphs and financial data, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Financial Obligations
scenes.line: It is used to estimate the relative likelihood that the individual will repay debts and meet other financial obligations. Credit scoring serves as a primary alternative to traditional forms of loan underwriting, enabling faster and more consistent credit decisions.
scenes.image_prompt: A calculator resting on top of a signed contract, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Free Report
scenes.line: Under the Dodd-Frank Act passed in 2010, a consumer is entitled to receive a free report of the specific credit score used if they are denied a loan, credit card or insurance. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau estimates that approximately 26 million Americans have no credit record with any of the three major credit bureaus.
scenes.image_prompt: A printed official government financial document on a desk, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Thin Records
scenes.line: An additional 19 million have records too thin or too stale to generate a score. Together these groups represent roughly 45 million adults who may be unable to access conventional credit products or qualify for loans on standard terms.
scenes.image_prompt: Old paper files stored inside metal filing cabinet drawers, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Demographic Impact
scenes.line: Credit invisibility disproportionately affects younger adults, Black and Hispanic consumers, and people in low-income neighborhoods. Before credit scores, credit was evaluated using credit reports from credit bureaus.
scenes.image_prompt: Busy pedestrians walking along a city sidewalk, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Computerized Scoring
scenes.line: During the late 1950s, banks started using computerized credit scoring to redefine creditworthiness as abstract statistical risk. The Equal Credit Opportunity Act banned denying credit on gender or marital status in 1974, along with race, nationality, religion, age, or receipt of public assistance in 1976.
scenes.image_prompt: Early mainframe computer equipment inside a brightly lit room, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Lawsuit Shield
scenes.line: Credit scoring adoption accelerated to shield against discrimination lawsuits. During the 1970s and 80s, the credit reporting industry relentlessly consolidated and moved aggressively into prescreening.
scenes.image_prompt: A set of heavy law books resting on a wooden shelf, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Mortgage Application
scenes.line: The FICO score burst into public consciousness in 1995 when Freddie Mac had lenders use credit scoring for all new mortgage applications. Modern credit scoring models date to 1958, when Bill Fair and Earl Isaac created Credit Application Scoring Algorithms, their first credit scoring system.
scenes.image_prompt: A suburban residential house viewed from the street, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: FICO Introduction
scenes.line: The FICO score was first introduced in 1989 by FICO, then called Fair, Isaac, and Company. The FICO model is used by the vast majority of banks and credit grantors, and is based on consumer credit files of the three national credit bureaus: Experian, Equifax, and TransUnion.
scenes.image_prompt: The exterior of a corporate office building, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Bureau Variations
scenes.line: Because a consumer credit file may contain different information at each of the companies, FICO scores can vary depending on which bureau provides the information. Credit scores are designed to measure the risk of default by taking into account various factors in a person financial history.
scenes.image_prompt: Three separate computer monitors displaying different financial charts, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Secret Formulas
scenes.line: Although the exact formulas for calculating credit scores are secret, FICO has disclosed the following components. Payment history accounts for 35 percent and is best described as the presence or lack of derogatory information.
scenes.image_prompt: A closed vintage metal safe with a combination dial, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Negative Events
scenes.line: Bankruptcy, settlements, charge-offs, repossessions, foreclosures, and late payments can cause a FICO score to drop. Debt burden accounts for 30 percent and considers a number of debt-specific measurements.
scenes.image_prompt: A stack of overdue utility bills and envelopes on a counter, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Debt Metrics
scenes.line: According to FICO there are six different metrics in the debt category including the debt to limit ratio and number of accounts with balances. Length of credit history or time in file accounts for 15 percent.
scenes.image_prompt: A close-up of a hand holding a modern smartphone, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: History Aging
scenes.line: As a credit history ages it can have a positive impact on its FICO score. There are several metrics in this category, most significantly the average age of the accounts on a report and the age of the oldest account.
scenes.image_prompt: A mature tree standing in a park during autumn, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Credit Types
scenes.line: Types of credit used accounts for 10 percent. Consumers can benefit by having a history of managing different types of credit.
scenes.image_prompt: A collection of different plastic credit and debit cards, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Recent Searches
scenes.line: Recent searches for credit account for 10 percent. Hard credit inquiries or hard pulls occur when consumers apply for a credit card or loan.
scenes.image_prompt: A person typing a search query on a laptop keyboard, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Inquiry Impact
scenes.line: Hard inquiries can hurt scores, especially if done in great numbers. Individuals who are rate shopping for a mortgage, auto loan, or student loan over a short period will likely not experience a meaningful decrease in their scores.
scenes.image_prompt: A red warning icon displayed on a digital dashboard, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Inquiry Grouping
scenes.line: The FICO scoring model considers all of those types of hard inquiries that occur within 14 or 45 days of each other as only one. Mortgage, auto, and student loan inquiries do not count at all in a FICO score if they are less than 30 days old.
scenes.image_prompt: A grouping of multiple file folders on a desk, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Display Period
scenes.line: All credit inquiries are recorded and displayed on personal credit reports for two years. They have no effect after the first year because FICO scoring system ignores them after 12 months.
scenes.image_prompt: A printed financial report showing historical data entries, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Soft Inquiries
scenes.line: Credit inquiries made by the consumer, by an employer, or by companies initiating pre-screened offers are called soft inquiries or soft pulls. Soft inquiries do not have any impact on a credit score and do not appear on a credit report used by lenders.
scenes.image_prompt: An unopened envelope sitting on a wooden hallway table, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Population Makeup
scenes.line: These percentages are based on the importance of the five categories for the general population. For particular groups, such as people who have not been using credit long, the relative importance of these categories may be different.
scenes.image_prompt: A diverse crowd of people walking down a busy city street, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Past Behavior
scenes.line: The makeup factors are limited to the individual past and continuing behavior on credit. Contrary to common misconception, other financial factors such as age, employment status, assets, or income are not accounted.
scenes.image_prompt: A person writing notes inside a small pocket notebook, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Lender Discretion
scenes.line: However, lenders are not prohibited from asking about and accounting these factors for particular lending considerations. Getting a higher credit limit can help a credit score.
scenes.image_prompt: A bank loan officer speaking across a meeting table, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Utilization Ratio
scenes.line: The higher the credit limit on the credit card, the lower the utilization ratio average for all of a borrower credit card accounts. The utilization ratio is the amount owed divided by the amount extended by the creditor.
scenes.image_prompt: A digital bar chart showing decreasing levels, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Court Judgments
scenes.line: Any money owed because of a court judgment or tax lien carries an additional penalty, especially when recent. Having one or more newly opened consumer finance credit accounts may also be a negative.
scenes.image_prompt: A wooden gavel resting on a matching sound block, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Score Range
scenes.line: The classic FICO credit score is between 300 and 850. 1.2 percent of Americans held the highest FICO score of 850 in 2019.
scenes.image_prompt: A gauge instrument showing a needle pointing upward, minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: National Bureaus
scenes.line: Each individual actually has over 60 credit scores for the FICO scoring model, as each of the three national credit bureaus has its own database, but the most used are 40. Data about an individual consumer can vary from bureau to bureau.
scenes.image_prompt: An office interior with computer servers and data processing equipment representing national credit bureaus., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Score Names
scenes.line: FICO scores have different names at each of the different credit reporting agencies: Equifax, TransUnion, and Experian. Equifax uses Beacon, TransUnion uses FICO Risk Score Classic, and Experian uses the Experian FICO Risk Model.
scenes.image_prompt: A modern corporate office lobby with three separate reception desks., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Active Generations
scenes.line: There are several active generations of FICO credit scores including FICO 98, FICO 04, FICO 8, FICO 9, FICO 10, and FICO 10T. A new type of FICO score named UltraFICO score was released in 2019.
scenes.image_prompt: A timeline chart displayed on a glass wall in a financial institution., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Inactive Scores
scenes.line: The FICO 95 credit score released in 1995 and Equifax FICO 98 scores are no longer in use. The Experian FICO 98 score is named FICO Score 2, and Experian FICO 04 score is FICO Score 3.
scenes.image_prompt: Old computer hardware stored neatly on metal shelving in a warehouse., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: TransUnion Renaming
scenes.line: TransUnion FICO 04 score is FICO Score 4, and Equifax FICO 04 score is FICO Score 5. The FICO Score XD is made with alternative data and was released in 2016.
scenes.image_prompt: A calculator and financial documents spread out on a clean workspace., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Mortgage Lenders
scenes.line: Mortgage lenders use EX FICO Score 2, EQ FICO Score 5 and TU FICO Score 4, but not a real FICO Mortgage Score. Consumers can buy their FICO scores plus credit report for Equifax, TransUnion, and Experian from the FICO website.
scenes.image_prompt: A desk with house keys resting on top of real estate loan paperwork., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Score Variety
scenes.line: They will get their FICO score 8, FICO Bankcard Score 8, FICO Auto Score 8, FICO Score 9, FICO Auto Score 9, and FICO Bankcard Score 9. Individuals can get up to 28 FICO scores on myFICO, consisting of 10 EX, 9 EQ, and 9 TU.
scenes.image_prompt: A stack of various consumer financial statements on a desk., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Experian Basic
scenes.line: Anyone can register and get their free EX FICO score 8 with Experian CreditWorks Basic. The FICO NextGen Risk Score is a scoring model designed by the FICO company for assessing consumer credit risk.
scenes.image_prompt: A person tapping a registration button on a digital tablet screen., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: NextGen Generations
scenes.line: This score was introduced in 2001, and in 2003 the second generation of NextGen was released. In 2004, FICO research showed a 4.4% increase in the number of accounts above cutoff compared to FICO traditional.
scenes.image_prompt: An office calendar hanging on a wall next to a window., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: NextGen Range
scenes.line: FICO NextGen score is between 150 and 950. Each of the major credit agencies markets this score generated with their data differently.
scenes.image_prompt: A digital meter graphic showing a numerical scale from 150 to 950., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: SBSS Score
scenes.line: The FICO Small Business Scoring Service score is used to evaluate small business credit applicants. This score can evaluate the personal credit report of a business owner along with the business credit report of the business itself.
scenes.image_prompt: A small business owner reviewing financial ledgers at a wooden desk., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: SBSS Range
scenes.line: The score range for the FICO SBSS score is 0 to 300, and a higher score indicates less risk. Applications for SBA 7(a) loans for $350,000 or less will be prescreened using this score.
scenes.image_prompt: A risk assessment gauge pointing toward a favorable green zone., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: VantageScore Intro
scenes.line: In 2006, the three major credit-reporting agencies introduced VantageScore credit score to try to win business away from FICO. According to court documents filed in the FICO v. VantageScore federal lawsuit, the VantageScore market share was less than 6% in 2006.
scenes.image_prompt: Corporate buildings in a financial district under an overcast sky., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: VantageScore Range
scenes.line: The VantageScore methodology initially produced a score range from 501 to 990. VantageScore 3.0 score adopted the score range of 300 to 850 in 2013.
scenes.image_prompt: An older computer terminal displaying a software numeric range., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: VantageScore 4.0
scenes.line: The VantageScore 4.0 score was released in mid-2017 and also uses a range of 300 to 850. Consumers can get free VantageScores from free credit report websites and from credit cards issued by major banks.
scenes.image_prompt: A software developer looking at code on a dual monitor workstation., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Vantage Tiers
scenes.line: The VantageScore 3.0 and 4.0 lower than 550 is very poor, 550 to 649 is poor, and 650 to 699 is fair. Vantage scores from 700 to 749 are good, and 750 to 850 are excellent.
scenes.image_prompt: A credit scoring tier chart printed on a laminated reference sheet., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Synchrony Usage
scenes.line: As of 2024, Synchrony Bank uses VantageScore 4.0 as the credit score for granting its credit cards. In July 2025, the Federal Housing Finance Agency announced that Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac will permit lenders to use VantageScore 4.0.
scenes.image_prompt: A plastic credit card resting on top of a retail purchase receipt., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: CE Score
scenes.line: CE Score is published by CE Analytics and is distributed to 6,500 lenders through the Credit Plus network with a range of 350 to 850. A number of scores have been developed to help consumers understand and improve their credit scores before FICO shared details.
scenes.image_prompt: A network server rack blinking with blue indicator lights in a data center., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: FAKO Scores
scenes.line: Discussions on the myFICO forum and elsewhere have referred to non-FICO scores as FAKO scores. Experian has the Plus Score between 330 and 830, and Experian's National Equivalence Score ranges from 360 to 840.
scenes.image_prompt: An online forum discussion board displayed on a computer screen., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Equifax Score
scenes.line: Equifax has the Equifax Credit Score of between 280 and 850. CreditXpert offers a simulation score to estimate the impact of various actions on a score range of 350 to 850.
scenes.image_prompt: A computer displaying a consumer credit summary report., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Alternative Data Usage
scenes.line: Lenders may choose to use non-FICO credit scores to gain additional insight on consumers with limited traditional credit history. Most of these scores are based significantly on data not available through the national credit bureaus.
scenes.image_prompt: A loan officer reviewing a non-traditional applicant file folder., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Credit Optics
scenes.line: The Credit Optics Score by SageStream blends traditional and alternative credit data with machine learning and ranges from 1 to 999. LexisNexis RiskView score, based on wide-ranging public records, ranges from 501 to 900.
scenes.image_prompt: Machine learning code and data curves displayed on a computer monitor., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: CoreLogic
scenes.line: CoreLogic Credco reports on property related public records and its Anthem Credit Score ranges from 325 to 850. PRBC allows consumers to self-enroll and report their own non-debt payment history with a range of 100 to 850.
scenes.image_prompt: Property deed documents and land survey maps resting on a desk., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: ChexSystems
scenes.line: There are also scores like ChexSystems Consumer Score designed for financial account verification services ranging from 100 to 899. Scorelogix LLC offers the JSS Credit Score, which assesses credit risk based on job history, income, and the impact of the economy.
scenes.image_prompt: A bank teller assisting a customer across a service counter., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Behavioral Risk
scenes.line: A Behavioral Risk Score from 0 to 999 is used by Comenity Bank and Comenity Capital Bank. TU CreditVision Scores and TU New Account score ranging from 300 to 850 are issued by TransUnion and used by WebBank.
scenes.image_prompt: A corporate banking office interior with minimalist desk setups., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Credit Builder
scenes.line: Credit builder loans offered by credit unions hold loan proceeds in a locked savings account while the borrower makes monthly payments. Since the mid-2010s, financial technology companies have offered comparable products through mobile applications without a membership requirement.
scenes.image_prompt: A traditional credit union building facade with glass doors., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Product Structure Mechanics
scenes.line: Product structure determines which scoring components are affected by reporting different types of consumer financial activity. Installment products report only installment activity and so build payment history alone without other categories.
scenes.image_prompt: A modern computer screen displaying financial graphs and data analysis charts., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Revolving Product Balances
scenes.line: Revolving products report a balance against a credit limit and therefore also generate a credit utilization ratio. The credit utilization ratio generated by revolving products forms a part of the debt burden category.
scenes.image_prompt: A credit card lying on top of printed bank statements in an office setting., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Rent and Bill Reporting
scenes.line: Rent and bill reporting adds existing recurring payments to a file rather than creating a new obligation. The effect of rent and bill reporting is limited by the specific scoring model evaluating the file.
scenes.image_prompt: A person reviewing monthly utility bills and rental payment receipts at home., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: VantageScore and FICO
scenes.line: VantageScore 4.0 and FICO 10T consider rent and utility payments while classic FICO scores do not. Classic FICO scores long used in mortgage underwriting do not consider rent and utility payments.
scenes.image_prompt: A computer monitor displaying comparative charts of different scoring algorithms., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Bureau Reach Issues
scenes.line: The effect is also limited by whether the payments reach the bureaus at all during the process. Payments reaching the bureaus was the case for about 13 percent of consumers in 2025.
scenes.image_prompt: A server room with glowing lights representing data transmission and network activity., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: CFPB Randomized Trial
scenes.line: In a randomized controlled trial of 1,531 credit union members commissioned by the CFPB, participants were evaluated. The randomized controlled trial was conducted by the RAND Corporation for the regulatory agency.
scenes.image_prompt: A researcher reviewing demographic data and clinical trial statistics on a laptop., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Credit Builder Loan Impact
scenes.line: Participants without existing debt saw modest score gains while those already carrying debt saw slight declines. Borrowers carrying existing debt became more likely to miss payments on their other loans during the trial.
scenes.image_prompt: A financial report highlighting contrasting upward and downward trend lines., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Late Payment Rates
scenes.line: Nearly 40 percent of borrowers made at least one late payment on the credit builder loan itself. As a result of the FACT Act, each legal U.S. resident is entitled to a free copy of their credit report.
scenes.image_prompt: A close-up of a hand holding a pen over a payment ledger., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Agency Report Frequency
scenes.line: Residents are entitled to a free copy of their credit report from each credit reporting agency once every twelve months. The law requires all three agencies, Equifax, Experian, and Transunion, to provide reports to consumers.
scenes.image_prompt: A calendar hanging on a wall showing monthly intervals., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Absence of Credit Scores
scenes.line: These credit reports do not contain credit scores from any of the three credit reporting agencies. The three credit bureaus run Annualcreditreport.com, where users can get their free credit reports.
scenes.image_prompt: A printed financial report page showing detailed text without any numerical score., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Add-On Credit Scores
scenes.line: Non-FICO credit scores are available as an add-on feature of the report for a fee. This fee is usually $7.95, as the FTC regulates this charge through the Fair Credit Reporting Act.
scenes.image_prompt: A digital checkout screen displaying an additional item charge., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: FTC Tracking Scams
scenes.line: The FTC tracks various scams and reports on other sites that provide fake credit reports. Instances of illegal behaviors by credit report services have been settled in court across the country.
scenes.image_prompt: A computer screen displaying cybersecurity warning alerts and data protection notices., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Experian Consumer Direct
scenes.line: Experian Consumer Direct was charged with deceptively signing people up for credit report monitoring services. The monitoring services charged consumers monthly fees through deceptive enrollment practices.
scenes.image_prompt: A corporate office building exterior with glass windows reflecting the sky., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Insurance Price Determination
scenes.line: Credit scores are often used in determining prices for auto and homeowner's insurance policies. Starting in the 1990s, national credit reporting agencies began generating more specialized insurance scores.
scenes.image_prompt: An insurance policy document lying next to a set of car keys on a table., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Insurance Risk Rating
scenes.line: Insurance companies use specialized scores to rate the insurance risk of potential customers. Studies indicate that the majority of those who are insured pay less in insurance through the use of scores.
scenes.image_prompt: An insurance agent reviewing risk assessment tables on a computer screen., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Claims Frequency Data
scenes.line: Studies point out that people with higher scores have fewer claims filed against their policies. In 2009, TransUnion representatives testified before the Connecticut legislature about marketing credit score reports.
scenes.image_prompt: A clipboard holding an insurance claim form and a pen on a desk., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Employer Hiring Use
scenes.line: TransUnion marketed credit score reports to employers for use in the hiring process. Legislators in at least twelve states introduced bills to limit the use of credit checks during hiring.
scenes.image_prompt: A desk with a resume, a notepad, and a professional pen ready for review., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Passed State Laws
scenes.line: Three states have passed laws to limit the use of credit checks during the hiring process. Credit scoring systems have garnered considerable criticism from various media outlets and debtors unions.
scenes.image_prompt: A state capitol building dome viewed against a clear daytime sky., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Consumer Law Concerns
scenes.line: Consumer law organizations and government officials raised concerns regarding the scoring system. Discrimination against prospective employees and rejection of rental applications are concerns raised.
scenes.image_prompt: Law books and legal briefs arranged neatly on a library bookshelf., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Racial Bias Concerns
scenes.line: Racial bias, poor risk prediction, manipulation of algorithms, and overall immorality are concerns. The scoring system has been studied as a form of classification to shape an individual's life-chances.
scenes.image_prompt: Abstract representation of digital code and complex algorithmic flowcharts on a screen., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Social Services Loss
scenes.line: The classification scheme is necessitated by the loss of collective social services and risk. The credit scoring system in the United States is similar to the Social Credit System in China.
scenes.image_prompt: An empty municipal office waiting room with closed service windows., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Basic Functions Criticism
scenes.line: Obtaining and maintaining employment, housing, transport, and insurance are basic functions of participation. Auto insurance and other basic needs are in some cases mandated by law for modern society.
scenes.image_prompt: A busy city street showing cars, pedestrians, and residential buildings in daylight., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: CFPB Deceit Charges
scenes.line: The CFPB charged Equifax and TransUnion with deliberate deceit of consumers about credit score values. Agencies were caught providing different scores to consumers than what was being provided to lenders.
scenes.image_prompt: A government regulatory notice document resting on an office desk., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Trial Service Fees
scenes.line: Agencies were charged with deceit by charging recurring fees to those enrolled in trial services. The credit reporting agencies were required to pay $23 million in fines and restitution.
scenes.image_prompt: A bank statement showing recurring monthly deductions highlighted in red marker., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

scenes.label: Data Breach Settlement
scenes.line: Equifax agreed to a settlement of $575 million with authorities related to a data breach. The data breach occurred in 2017 where 147 million people were affected by exposed information.
scenes.image_prompt: A secure server rack in a data center with indicator lights flashing., minimalist flat vector illustration, clean modern financial infographics, dark slate and emerald green color palette, professional aesthetic

long_how_credit_scores_quietly_determine.source_title: Credit score in the United States

long_how_inflation_secretly_reduces_your.title: How Inflation Secretly Reduces Your Money's Purchasing Power

scenes.label: Astonishing Fact
scenes.line: One of the earliest documented inflations occurred in Alexander the Great's empire 330 BC. How does an increase in the general price level reduce the purchasing power of money?

scenes.label: Term Origin
